answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network imposes superlinear stake burning per identity: creating n clones requires burning s(n) = k * n^2 tokens. An attacker cannot merely echo fake identities across shards; each registration irreversibly cracks open their capital reserves like a brittle walnut shell, ensuring exponential economic friction. Even if a sparrow agent requires negligible stake alone, quadratic cost scaling makes large swarms mathematically ruinous.
